newsitem.title: UK: Costly new Rolls undermines Vickers.
newsitem.headline: Costly new Rolls undermines Vickers.

text.p: British auto and defence manufacturer Vickers Plc posted a gain in half-year profits on Thursday but admitted it was still struggling to offset the high investment costs required for a new Rolls-Royce car and to get on top of some of its markets.

The group reported an 18 percent rise in first-half pretax profit to 31.8 million pounds ($50 million), and said it was confident of being able to make further earnings progress in the second half of the year.

It acknowleged, however, that profit margins in its high-profile automotive businesses, including Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars and its specialist engineering firm Cosworth, were pressured both by high investment costs and mixed markets.

Analysts expressed concern at the slow prospects for new tank orders for Vickers' defence systems division, which Chief Executive Sir Colin Chandler said was "out there fighting" for prospective Middle Eastern orders, in particular.
Chandler said in an interview he was quietly confident in the company's overall performance but repeated his often-heard warning that "one shouldn't stoke up too many expectations."
Within an 11 percent rise in total group sales, to 554 million pounds ($865 million), Rolls Royce Motor Cars posted a 26 percent sales rise in the period.
However, Chandler said the unit was under some pressure as it spends on engineering and tooling for its new product line.
"We are investing a lot at the moment...when doing that we obviously are not getting a very good return on sales," he said in a telephone interview.
Going forward, he added, Rolls's sales prospects would be dependent on the rate of increase of global GDP, which on current forecasts appears to be on a steady course.

"I think we'll see pretty steady growth," he said, though he added Vickers expected the new four-door Bentley and Rolls-Royce model range would spur along sales and allow them to break out of the expected gentle uptrend.
